title: Add clickable week numbers to the calendar's month view (jump to week view, matching existing date-to-day drill-down)
tech: React + TypeScript frontend only -- react-big-calendar (already installed, v1.20.0) + Luxon (already installed and already used throughout AdminCalendar.tsx), no new dependency expected
keyConstraints: Current behavior, confirmed by reading AdminCalendar.tsx: no onDrillDown prop is set on the <Calendar>, so clicking a date number in Month view to jump to Day view is entirely react-big-calendar's own default drill-down behavior (its default onDrillDown handler switches to drilldownView, which defaults to Day when unset) -- this app has never customized it. There is no equivalent gesture for jumping to Week view today. Investigated react-big-calendar v1.20.0's actual type definitions (node_modules/@types/react-big-calendar/index.d.ts): onDrillDown?: (date: Date, view: View) => void and drilldownView?: View | null are real, overridable top-level Calendar props -- but the Components interface (same file, ~line 200-241) has no per-week-row header slot at all, only month.header (per weekday COLUMN, e.g. 'Sun'/'Mon' labels, once each) and month.dateHeader (per individual date CELL, e.g. the '15' in a day cell). There is no built-in place to render 'a label for this whole row.' The most viable extension point for adding a week-number indicator is components.dateCellWrapper (wraps each individual date cell) -- rendering a week-number badge only on the first cell of each week row (i.e. where the cell's date is a Sunday, matching react-big-calendar's default week-start) is the likely approach, but DateCellWrapperProps's exact shape/rendering contract (whether it wraps-and-passes-through children vs. replaces them, and whether adding sibling content breaks the library's internal event-positioning math for that cell) has not been verified and must be confirmed by Architect before committing to this approach -- this project has a track record (task 020) of discovering a library's real capabilities don't match what the task assumed, and pivoting; don't assume dateCellWrapper works as hoped without checking react-big-calendar's actual Month.js/DateContentRow.js source for how it's consumed. If dateCellWrapper turns out not to be viable for this without fighting the library's layout internals, Architect should propose the next-best alternative (e.g. a small, separate 'jump to week' control positioned near the calendar rather than injected into its grid) rather than force a fragile integration. Week-number computation should use Luxon's DateTime.weekNumber (ISO week number) -- already the date library in use throughout this file, no new dependency. Custom onDrillDown, if used for the date-to-day behavior, must preserve the EXISTING default behavior exactly (date click still jumps to Day view for that date) -- this is additive (add week-number-click-to-Week-view), not a replacement of existing behavior.
description: In the calendar's Month view, add a visible week number for each row, clickable to jump directly to Week view for that week -- mirroring the existing (default, library-provided) behavior where clicking a date number jumps to Day view for that date. This gives the masseur a fast way to see a whole week's bookings/availability without manually switching to Week view and navigating forward/back to the right week.
acceptanceCriteria: Month view displays a week number for each visible row (ISO week number, via Luxon's DateTime.weekNumber)
Clicking/tapping a week number switches the calendar to Week view, navigated to that week
Existing behavior -- clicking a date number still jumps to Day view for that date -- is unchanged
The week-number control is clearly a distinct, clickable element (not confusable with a date cell), verified at a narrow (phone-width) viewport

No regression to any existing AdminCalendar test (booking rendering/actions, blocked-day rendering in View and Manage mode, batch-block, toolbar) -- run the full existing suite, not just an assumed-safe subset
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in frontend/ (backend should be unaffected since no backend files change)
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.tsx (the Calendar component and its props)
frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.css (styling for the new week-number element)
frontend/test/AdminCalendar.test.tsx (new test coverage for the jump-to-week interaction; full suite must keep passing)

frontend/node_modules/@types/react-big-calendar/index.d.ts (read-only reference -- confirms onDrillDown/drilldownView/Components shape; Architect should also check the actual .js source in frontend/node_modules/react-big-calendar/lib/ for how dateCellWrapper and Month view rows are really implemented before committing to an approach)
securityConsiderations: None -- purely client-side navigation/view-state change, no new data, no new API calls.
